title: Less mass
coreMove: Treat every commitment as weight that raises the force to change later; keep mass low so a mistake stays cheap to undo and a new priority does not drag a machine behind it.

exampleSpecs.audience: founders equating long contracts with seriousness
exampleSpecs.stakes: sign a long lease or keep the company able to move
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist treats a long contract as mass that resists change

exampleSpecs.audience: teams tempted to build heavy custom systems early
exampleSpecs.stakes: build custom code or rent a tool that teaches the same thing
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist applies the smaller-promise test before adding mass

exampleSpecs.audience: leaders attached to a decision that no longer works
exampleSpecs.stakes: defend a proud past call or drop the dead weight
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist counts pride as mass alongside physical assets

exampleSpecs.audience: founders confusing lightness with refusing to commit
exampleSpecs.stakes: commit on purpose or refuse everything and stall
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist separates useful structure from dead weight

exampleSpecs.audience: teams choosing how much to take on at the earliest stage
exampleSpecs.stakes: match a bigger rival's footprint or stay deliberately lean
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist keeps fewer features, people, and obligations to stay agile

exampleSpecs.audience: leaders assuming scale improves error correction
exampleSpecs.stakes: carry heavy mass for safety or stay light to fix mistakes cheaply
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: low mass makes the same mistake cheaper to undo
